# blendops-camera

Purpose: Plan camera, composition, resolution, and aspect ratio, and check framing quality against written criteria.

Metadata: Contract `v2.0.0` | Category `scene-planners` | Role `camera-composition-framing-and-aspect-planner` | Tier `L0` | Runtime default `Not Run` | Artifact default `Not Produced` | Mutation `downgrade_only`

## When to use & trigger cues
- Camera angle, lens, or framing needs a plan.
- Resolution or aspect ratio must match a delivery target.
- Composition needs a check against written criteria.
- Trigger phrases: "improve composition and camera", "choose hero framing", "set camera strategy for product hero", "is the framing okay", "check composition", "subject feels off-center", "too much negative space", "what resolution", "how big should the render be", "16:9 or square"

## When not to use (delegation boundaries)
- to design lighting rigs or surface materials/lookdev → use `blendops-lighting-materials` (`references/skill-blendops-lighting-materials.md`; use blendops-lighting-materials)
- to choose delivery file formats → use `blendops-render-settings` (`references/skill-blendops-render-settings.md`; use blendops-render-settings)
- when subject intent is undefined → use `blendops-product-shot` (`references/skill-blendops-product-shot.md`; Delegates out-of-scope requests to blendops-product-shot)
- material validation → use `blendops-lighting-materials` (`references/skill-blendops-lighting-materials.md`; use blendops-lighting-materials)
- lighting validation → use `blendops-lighting-materials` (`references/skill-blendops-lighting-materials.md`; use blendops-lighting-materials)
- broad scene Pass/Warn/Fail readiness review → use `blendops-final-check` (`references/skill-blendops-final-check.md`; use blendops-final-check)
- classifying render or export artifact evidence → use `blendops-final-check` (`references/skill-blendops-final-check.md`; use blendops-final-check)
- pure modeling → use `blendops-render-settings` (`references/skill-blendops-render-settings.md`; Delegates out-of-scope requests to blendops-render-settings)

## Input & output contract
- Required input `domain_scene_plan` (`object`): Upstream scene layout plan defining subject scale, staging, and depth layers
- Required input `framing_goal` (`string`): Target shot type (hero three-quarter, orthographic catalog grid, portrait, wide establishing)
- Optional input `pinned_aspect_ratio` (`string`): Aspect ratio lock from blendops-camera
- Optional input `camera_and_framing_spec` (`object`): Camera focal length, sensor, angle, and subject placement from blendops-camera
- Optional input `pinned_aspect_ratio_and_subject` (`object`): Locked aspect ratio and primary/secondary focal hierarchy from brief
- Optional input `viewport_or_render_preview_notes` (`string`): Optional framing observations from a viewport or preview capture
- Optional input `target_delivery_surfaces` (`array`): Target display placements (desktop hero banner, mobile portrait feed, 1:1 e-commerce card, 4K print)
- Optional input `framing_and_crop_strategy` (`string`): Whether deliverables use a single master aspect ratio with safe-zone crops or separate camera setups
- Optional input `render_time_constraints` (`string`): Optional render time ceiling influencing pixel dimensions and percentage scale
- Output contract: `camera_rig_specification`, `focal_length_and_dof_plan`, `composition_anchor_guidelines`, `composition_verdict_table`, `silhouette_and_headroom_assessment`, `camera_replan_remediation_hints`, `pinned_pixel_dimensions_and_aspect_ratio`, `safe_frame_and_overscan_margins`, `camera_sensor_fit_alignment_notes` (Runtime status: `Not Run`, Artifact status: `Not Produced`, `downgrade_only`).

## Safety boundaries & non-goals
- Runtime boundary: BlendOps runtime guidance uses **2 MCP execution paths plus a CLI fallback appendix** (replaces older 3-stack and 4-route drafts — see `docs/runtime-stack-strategy.md` for the corrected attribution history):
- Does not install Blender, configure an MCP bridge, or own a runtime; it points to upstream paths only.
- Does not claim render, export, preview, or GLB results without evidence.
- Does not hand the user Python as the final interface.
